title: Graze your way through Adelaide Central Market
description: One of the largest undercover produce markets in the Southern Hemisphere - cheese, smallgoods, doughnuts and a coffee crawl in one building.

title: Find the Mall's Balls and the bronze pigs on Rundle Mall
description: Adelaide's pedestrian shopping street, worth it for the buskers and the four bronze pigs rummaging in a bin.

title: Walk the Bicentennial Conservatory at Adelaide Botanic Garden
description: Free 51-hectare garden in the middle of the city, with a giant glasshouse of lowland rainforest and the Museum of Economic Botany.

title: Spend a rainy afternoon in the Art Gallery of South Australia
description: Free entry to a serious collection of Australian, Aboriginal and European art on North Terrace.

title: See the Australian Aboriginal Cultures Gallery at the SA Museum
description: Home to the world's most comprehensive collection of Australian Aboriginal cultural material, plus the opal and megafauna halls.

title: Climb the Adelaide Oval roof at sunset
description: A harnessed walk along the stadium roofline, 50m above the pitch, with the city and the Adelaide Hills laid out around you.

title: Visit the giant pandas at Adelaide Zoo
description: Australia's second-oldest zoo and the only one in the country to host giant pandas.

title: Ride the tram to Glenelg for fish and chips on the jetty
description: The historic tram runs from the city centre straight to Jetty Road and a wide swimming beach - the classic Adelaide afternoon.

title: Watch the sun drop into the sea at Henley Beach Square
description: West-facing beach where the whole square turns out for sunset - grab a table and watch it go down over the Gulf.

title: Ride the Semaphore miniature steam railway
description: An old-fashioned seaside strip with a working miniature railway along the foreshore and a long, calm swimming beach.

title: Spot dolphins on a Port River cruise
description: A resident population of bottlenose dolphins lives in the Port River, alongside the ship graveyard and the old maritime warehouses.

title: Climb inside a Bluebird railcar at the National Railway Museum
description: The largest railway museum in Australia, in Port Adelaide - huge steam locomotives you can walk through.

title: Hike to all three waterfalls in Morialta
description: A steep gorge 20 minutes from the CBD with three waterfalls and a good chance of koalas in the gums.

title: Hold a koala at Cleland Wildlife Park
description: One of the few places in Australia where you can legally hold a koala, plus walk-through kangaroo and emu enclosures.

title: See all of Adelaide from the Mount Lofty Summit
description: 727m lookout taking in the entire city, the Gulf and the Hills - best an hour before sunset.

title: Eat pork knuckle in Hahndorf, Australia's oldest German town
description: Settled by Prussian Lutherans in 1839 - a main street of German bakeries, beer halls and the Hahndorf Academy.

title: See the autumn colour in Stirling
description: A Hills village planted with European deciduous trees - in April and May the whole main street turns red and gold.

title: Drive your car onto the sand at Aldinga Beach
description: One of the few beaches in SA where you can legally drive onto the sand and park facing the water.

title: Photograph the old jetty ruins at Port Willunga
description: Weathered jetty pylons standing in the shallows below limestone cliffs and the cave-cut boat sheds - the best sunset on the Fleurieu.

title: Do a Shiraz tasting flight in McLaren Vale
description: Old-vine Shiraz and Grenache country 45 minutes from Adelaide, with cellar doors between the vines and the sea.

title: Get lost in the Alternate Realities Museum at the d'Arenberg Cube
description: A five-storey Rubik's-cube building dropped into a McLaren Vale vineyard, part cellar door, part surrealist art museum.

title: Walk beneath the red cliffs at Maslin Beach
description: Dramatic banded ochre cliffs above a long beach - Australia's first legal nude beach occupies the southern end.

title: Take the horse-drawn tram to Granite Island at Victor Harbor
description: A Clydesdale still pulls a double-decker tram across the causeway - the last horse-drawn tram of its kind in the world.

title: Walk the Kaiki Trail around Granite Island
description: A 1.5km loop over pink granite boulders with fur seals on the rocks and whales offshore in winter.

title: Watch southern right whales calving in Encounter Bay
description: Southern right whales come into the bay to calve every winter - the Bluff and Rosetta Head are the free viewing spots.

title: Hike down to Deep Creek Waterfall
description: The wildest corner of the Fleurieu - steep gullies down to hidden beaches, with a serious climb back out.

title: Catch the ferry from Cape Jervis to Kangaroo Island
description: The 45-minute crossing of Backstairs Passage - book the car on early, it fills up over summer.

title: Spend three days circling Kangaroo Island
description: Australia's third-largest island - sea lions, koalas, wild coastline and dark skies, an hour off the mainland.

title: Walk the beach among wild sea lions at Seal Bay
description: A guided walk onto the sand of a working Australian sea lion colony - one of the only places on earth you can do this.

title: Watch first light hit the Remarkable Rocks
description: Wind-carved granite boulders balanced on a dome 75m above the Southern Ocean, orange with lichen at sunrise.

title: Count the fur seals under Admirals Arch
description: A collapsed sea cave hung with stalactites at Cape du Couedic, with hundreds of long-nosed fur seals on the rocks below.

title: See the regrowth after the fires in Flinders Chase
description: The wild western end of Kangaroo Island - badly burnt in 2019-20 and now a remarkable study in how mallee country comes back.

title: Watch the evening pelican feed at Kingscote wharf
description: Kangaroo Island's main town, with a long-running pelican feed on the town jetty.

title: Swim off the jetty at Emu Bay
description: A 5km north-facing white sand beach with calm water - one of the few KI beaches you can drive onto.

title: Watch little penguins come ashore at Penneshaw
description: The ferry town, with a little penguin colony that comes up the rocks after dark.

title: Ride the shuttle past the lions at Monarto Safari Park
description: The largest open-range zoo outside Africa - 1,500 hectares of white rhino, giraffe, cheetah and lions an hour from Adelaide.

title: Taste 100-year-old vine Shiraz in the Barossa
description: Australia's most famous wine region, with some of the oldest continuously producing Shiraz vines on the planet.

title: Buy mettwurst from a Tanunda butcher
description: The most German of the Barossa towns - Lutheran churches, bakeries and butchers still making mettwurst the old way.

title: Stand in the original Grange cellar at Penfolds Magill Estate
description: The birthplace of Penfolds Grange, still a working vineyard inside Adelaide's suburbs - 20 minutes from the CBD.

title: Drink Riesling where it grows best in the Clare Valley
description: Two hours north of Adelaide and Australia's benchmark Riesling country, quieter and greener than the Barossa.

title: Cycle the Riesling Trail between cellar doors
description: 35km of old railway line converted to a flat gravel path, with cellar doors the whole way along it.

title: Buy the Burra Passport key and let yourself into the historic sites
description: A 19th-century copper town where a single key unlocks eight heritage sites, including the dugouts miners lived in on the creek bank.

title: Tour the Georgian rooms of Martindale Hall at Mintaro
description: An 1880 mansion used as the school in Picnic at Hanging Rock, in a slate-quarry village of about 80 people.

title: Stay a night in the Clare township
description: The valley's main town and the practical base for a weekend of Riesling and the Trail.

title: Follow the Copper Coast trail through Cornish mining country
description: Wallaroo, Moonta and Kadina - the Little Cornwall triangle, built on 19th-century copper and still holding the Kernewek Lowender festival.

title: Eat a Cornish pasty on the Wallaroo foreshore
description: A working grain port with a long jetty, a swimming beach and bakeries that still take the pasty seriously.

title: Ride the Moonta Mines tourist railway through the ruins
description: Once the richest copper mine in Australia - a small train runs through the ruins, tailings and Miners' Cottage.

title: Find the Ethel shipwreck on the beach at Innes National Park
description: The wild toe of Yorke Peninsula - surf breaks, the ghost town of Inneston and the rusted ribs of a wreck in the sand.

title: Watch the sun set over the Southern Ocean at Marion Bay
description: The last town before Innes, with a beach that faces straight into the Southern Ocean swell.

title: Drive the full loop of the Yorke Peninsula
description: A boot-shaped peninsula of crayfish, jetties and empty beaches that most interstate visitors drive straight past.

title: Shuck Coffin Bay oysters standing in the water they grew in
description: Wader-deep oyster tours where you stand at a table in the lease and eat them straight out of the bay.

title: Four-wheel-drive out to Point Sir Isaac
description: Soft-sand tracks out along a remote peninsula of dunes and emerald bays - genuine 4WD country, not a soft-roader run.

title: Cage-dive with great white sharks out of Port Lincoln
description: The only place in Australia licensed for great white cage diving, out at the Neptune Islands.

title: Swim with wild sea lions at Baird Bay
description: A tiny fishing settlement where one family-run operation takes you into the water with a wild sea lion colony that comes to play.

title: Drive the Seafood Frontier around the Eyre Peninsula
description: Oysters at Coffin Bay, tuna at Port Lincoln, whiting all the way up the west coast - Australia's best-value seafood drive.

title: Look down on whales from the cliffs at Head of Bight
description: Southern right whales calve directly below the Bunda Cliffs here - the best land-based whale watching in Australia.

title: Stand on the salt crust of Lake Gairdner
description: A 160km salt lake used for land speed record attempts - blinding white to the horizon and almost nobody there.

title: Sleep under the stars in the Flinders Ranges
description: 800-million-year-old ranges of red rock, river red gums and yellow-footed rock wallabies, five hours north of Adelaide.

title: Climb toward St Mary Peak on the rim of Wilpena Pound
description: A 21km circuit around a natural amphitheatre 17km long. Adnyamathanha Traditional Owners ask that walkers stop below the actual summit.

title: Go underground at Blinman, the highest town in South Australia
description: Population about 20, elevation 610m - a guided underground tour of a copper mine that closed in 1907.

title: Look through the telescopes at Arkaroola's observatories
description: A private wilderness sanctuary in the northern Flinders with three observatories and some of the darkest skies in Australia.

title: Eat feral food at the Prairie Hotel in Parachilna
description: A pub in a town of almost nobody, famous for a mixed grill of camel, kangaroo and emu.

title: Ride the Pichi Richi steam train out of Quorn
description: Original Ghan locomotives running the 1879 line through the Pichi Richi Pass, restored and operated by volunteers.

title: Ride the mountain bike trails at Melrose
description: The oldest town in the Flinders and now the state's mountain biking capital, with trails starting off the main street.

title: Walk the floor of Alligator Gorge
description: A narrow red quartzite gorge where the walls close in to a few metres apart - you walk along the creek bed between them.

title: See megafauna fossils at the Naracoorte Caves
description: South Australia's only World Heritage site - pitfall caves that trapped and preserved 500,000 years of Australian megafauna.

title: Walk the Obelisk track at Robe
description: A red-and-white striped obelisk on eroding limestone cliffs, above a town of crayfish boats and long beaches.

title: Float in the Pool of Siloam at Beachport
description: A saltwater lake around seven times saltier than the sea - you physically cannot sink in it.

title: See the Blue Lake turn cobalt at Mount Gambier
description: A crater lake that shifts from steel grey to brilliant cobalt every November and back again in March, for reasons still debated.

title: Canoe the Coorong lagoons
description: A 130km saltwater lagoon behind the Younghusband Peninsula dunes, Ngarrindjeri country and the setting for Storm Boy.

title: Take a paddle steamer out of Mannum
description: The birthplace of the Murray River paddle steamer trade, an hour from Adelaide, with houseboats and limestone cliffs.

title: Follow the street art down Hosier Lane and AC/DC Lane
description: Melbourne's bluestone laneways repaint themselves constantly - Hosier, Rutledge, AC/DC and Centre Place, with coffee at every turn.

title: Meet under the big screen at Federation Square
description: Melbourne's divisive sandstone-and-zinc civic square, and the front door to ACMI and the Ian Potter Centre.

title: Do a winter night market lap of Queen Victoria Market
description: Seven hectares of open-air market trading since 1878, with a hot-food night market in winter and again in summer.

title: Stand under the stained-glass ceiling at NGV International
description: The oldest and most visited gallery in Australia - walk through the water wall and lie on the floor under Leonard French's ceiling.

title: See Phar Lap at the Melbourne Museum
description: Home to the mounted hide of Phar Lap, a living forest gallery and the Bunjilaka Aboriginal Cultural Centre.

title: Walk the treetop gorilla trail at Melbourne Zoo
description: Australia's oldest zoo, ten minutes from the city by tram, with summer twilight concerts on the lawn.

title: Stand in the penguin snow room at SEA LIFE Melbourne
description: A city-centre aquarium on the Yarra with king and gentoo penguins in a genuinely cold sub-Antarctic enclosure.

title: Do the Aboriginal Heritage Walk at the Royal Botanic Gardens
description: 38 hectares beside the Yarra, with a guided walk led by an Aboriginal guide through plants used on Kulin country.

title: Watch the little penguins come home at the St Kilda breakwater
description: A wild little penguin colony living in the rocks of the pier breakwater, ten minutes from the CBD and completely free.

title: Ride the Scenic Railway through Luna Park's giant mouth
description: Open since 1912, and its Scenic Railway is the oldest continually operating rollercoaster in the world - still with a brakeman riding along.

title: Photograph the 82 Brighton Bathing Boxes
description: A row of Victorian-era timber boxes on Dendy Street Beach, each individually owned, painted and worth more than a house in some towns.

title: Row a boat or kayak the Yarra through the city
description: Paddling the Yarra puts you below the skyline and the Boathouse Drive rowing sheds - a different city from the one on the bank.

title: Ride Puffing Billy with your legs over the side
description: An 1900 narrow-gauge steam railway through the Dandenongs - the one train where sitting on the windowsill is the point.

title: Walk the 1,000 Steps Kokoda Track Memorial Walk
description: A steep climb through mountain ash and tree ferns, built as a memorial to the Kokoda campaign.

title: See a platypus up close at Healesville Sanctuary
description: An all-Australian-species sanctuary in the Yarra Valley bush, with a platypus enclosure and a free-flight raptor show.

title: Float over the Yarra Valley in a dawn hot air balloon
description: Balloons lift at first light over Victoria's cool-climate Chardonnay and Pinot country, landing in time for a winery breakfast.

title: Get lost in the Arthurs Seat maze on the Mornington Peninsula
description: An hour from Melbourne - a hook of vineyards, hot springs, calm bay beaches and surf coast on the other side.

title: Catch the Sorrento to Queenscliff ferry across the Heads
description: A 40-minute crossing of the Rip that saves a three-hour drive, with dolphins alongside more often than not.

title: Walk out to Fort Nepean where Australia fired the first shot of WWI
description: Gun emplacements and tunnels at the very tip of the peninsula, which fired on a German steamer hours after war was declared in 1914.

title: Sit in the hilltop pool at Peninsula Hot Springs after dark
description: Geothermal water piped into more than 70 pools - the hilltop bath at night, in winter, is the one everybody remembers.

title: Do a lap of the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit
description: You can ride the circuit as a hot-lap passenger or drive a go-kart replica of one of the great MotoGP tracks.

title: Sit on the sand for the Penguin Parade
description: Hundreds of little penguins surf in at dusk and walk up the beach past you - book, and dress far warmer than you think.

title: Walk the boardwalk over the blowhole at the Nobbies
description: The western tip of Phillip Island, above Australia's largest fur seal colony out on Seal Rocks.

title: Watch the working sheepdogs on Churchill Island
description: The site of the first European crop planted in Victoria, now a heritage farm with daily whip-cracking and dog demonstrations.

title: Spend a weekend at Wilsons Promontory, the mainland's southern tip
description: Granite headlands, wombats on the roads and some of the whitest sand in the country - book Tidal River months in advance.

title: Hear the sand squeak underfoot at Squeaky Beach
description: Rounded quartz grains that genuinely squeak when you walk on them, between orange granite boulders.

title: Camp at Tidal River and watch the wombats come out
description: The Prom's only campground, on a tannin-stained river behind Norman Beach - ballot-allocated over summer.

title: Climb Mount Oberon for sunset over the Prom
description: A 6.8km return climb on a management vehicle track to a 360-degree view over the whole peninsula and its islands.

title: Drive the Great Ocean Road end to end
description: 243km built by returned WWI soldiers as the world's largest war memorial - do it west to east so you are on the ocean side.

title: Watch sunrise at the Twelve Apostles before the buses arrive
description: Limestone stacks left behind as the cliffs eroded - there are eight standing now, and dawn is the only quiet hour.

title: Walk down into Loch Ard Gorge
description: Named for an 1878 wreck from which only two teenagers survived, washing into this narrow beach between the cliffs.

title: Stand on the beach beneath the cliffs at Gibson Steps
description: 86 steps cut into the cliff face let you stand at the base of the stacks - the only place you see them from below. Check the tide.

title: Spot glow worms and wild koalas in the Otways
description: Cool temperate rainforest of myrtle beech and tree ferns behind the coast, with the country's most reliable wild koala spotting near Kennett River.

title: Walk the Maits Rest rainforest boardwalk
description: A 30-minute loop among 300-year-old myrtle beech and hollow mountain ash - the easiest genuine rainforest walk in Victoria.

title: Walk to Erskine Falls behind Lorne
description: A 30m waterfall in fern gully ten minutes inland from the Great Ocean Road's most popular beach town.

title: Eat fish straight off the boat at Apollo Bay harbour
description: A working fishing harbour where the co-op sells the catch, between the Otway hills and the sea.

title: Explore Gariwerd, the Grampians
description: Sandstone ranges rising out of flat farmland, holding the largest concentration of Aboriginal rock art in southern Australia.

title: Descend to the base of MacKenzie Falls
description: One of the few Victorian falls that runs all year - a steep staircase down to the spray at the bottom, and a hard climb back.

title: Squeeze through the Grand Canyon to The Pinnacle
description: A scramble through slot canyons and boulder tunnels to a railed rock platform hanging over the Halls Gap valley.

title: Watch the kangaroos take over Halls Gap at dusk
description: The Grampians' base town, where mobs of eastern grey kangaroos graze the oval and caravan park every evening.

title: Pan for real gold at Ballarat
description: The heart of the 1850s gold rush and the Eureka Stockade, with grand streetscapes built on the proceeds.

title: Watch the gold pour at Sovereign Hill
description: A full-scale working 1850s goldfields town where they pour a real gold ingot daily and you can go down a mine shaft.

title: Ride the vintage talking tram through Bendigo
description: Gold-boom architecture on a scale that seems absurd for the town's size, plus the Central Deborah Mine 61m underground.

title: Catch a blockbuster exhibition at Bendigo Art Gallery
description: One of Australia's oldest regional galleries, which regularly lands international fashion and design exhibitions no other regional city gets.

title: Board a working paddle steamer at Echuca wharf
description: The largest collection of operating paddle steamers in the world, at a red gum wharf built when this was Australia's busiest inland port.

title: Hire a houseboat on the Murray for a few nights
description: Australia's longest river, lined with river red gums - you drive the boat yourself and tie up to the bank wherever you like.

title: See the night sound-and-light show at Swan Hill Pioneer Settlement
description: A recreated river port town, with an after-dark laser show projected across the settlement and the Murray.

title: Taste 100-year-old Muscat in Rutherglen
description: Fortified wine country - Rutherglen Muscat and Topaque are among the very few wine styles Australia genuinely leads the world in.

title: Stand in Ned Kelly's cell at the Beechworth Gaol
description: An almost perfectly preserved gold town where the Kelly family were repeatedly tried - plus a very good bakery and brewery.

title: Walk under the autumn trees in Bright
description: An alpine town planted with elms, oaks and maples that turns spectacular for about three weeks every April.

title: Walk out to the Horn on Mount Buffalo
description: A granite plateau of tors, snow gums and the Gorge - Victoria's oldest alpine park and much quieter than the ski resorts.

title: Ski or snowshoe at Falls Creek
description: Victoria's largest alpine resort, ski-in ski-out, and in summer one of the best mountain biking areas in the country.

title: Drive the Great Alpine Road over Mount Hotham
description: The highest year-round sealed road in Australia, running along a ridgeline through snow gum country.

title: Take the waters at Daylesford
description: The centre of Australia's largest concentration of mineral springs, and a weekend town of bathhouses, bakeries and Lake Daylesford.

title: Pump your own mineral water at Hepburn Springs
description: Free public hand pumps in the Mineral Springs Reserve - bring a bottle and taste the difference between each spring.

title: See a show at the Castlemaine Theatre Royal
description: A goldfields town turned arts town, with one of the oldest continuously operating theatres on the Australian mainland.

title: Stand inside the Great Stupa of Universal Compassion
description: A 50m Tibetan Buddhist stupa rising out of the bush near Bendigo, holding the Jade Buddha for Universal Peace.

title: Take a boat out to Skull Rock off Wilsons Promontory
description: Cleft Island - a granite dome with a 130m cave mouth like an eye socket, reachable only by boat on a calm day.

title: Wander the Dimboola Imaginarium
description: A gloriously strange gallery, curiosity shop and cafe in a tiny Wimmera town most people only see from the highway.

title: Photograph the Giant Koala at Dadswells Bridge
description: A 14m concrete koala on the Western Highway, and a properly good entry in Australia's Big Things canon.

title: Tick off the Big Wine Bottle at Rutherglen
description: A converted water tower painted as a giant bottle - the Big Thing that marks the entrance to fortified wine country.

title: Cross the Murray from Wodonga into New South Wales on foot
description: The Victorian half of the Albury-Wodonga border twin towns - you can walk over the river and change states mid-bridge.

title: Walk the Griffiths Island lighthouse loop at Port Fairy
description: A whitewashed fishing village at the quiet end of the coast, with a short-tailed shearwater colony on the island each summer.

title: Walk into a dormant volcano at Tower Hill
description: A nest of volcanic cones inside a crater lake, replanted from a Eugene von Guerard painting and now full of emus and koalas.

title: Kayak the Mallacoota inlet
description: A remote town at the far eastern corner of Victoria, on a huge quiet inlet between Croajingolong wilderness and the sea.

title: Sail the Gippsland Lakes and cross to Ninety Mile Beach
description: The largest inland waterway network in Australia, separated from the ocean by a single long dune of Ninety Mile Beach.

title: See a performance inside the Sydney Opera House
description: Utzon's World Heritage shells are worth seeing from the inside - the Concert Hall reopened in 2022 after a major acoustic rebuild.

title: Climb the arch of the Sydney Harbour Bridge
description: 134m above the water on the arch of the Coathanger. The pedestrian walkway underneath is free if the climb price stings.

title: Walk to Mrs Macquarie's Chair through the Royal Botanic Garden
description: Free harbourside gardens on Gadigal land since 1816, ending at the sandstone bench with the classic Opera House and Bridge view.

title: Drink in the oldest pubs in The Rocks
description: Convict-era sandstone lanes under the bridge, with a weekend market and several pubs each claiming to be Sydney's oldest.

title: Walk the sandstone headland at Barangaroo Reserve
description: A container terminal rebuilt into a naturalistic headland from 10,000 hand-cut sandstone blocks, named for a Cammeraygal woman.

title: Swim between the flags at Bondi Beach
description: Australia's most famous kilometre of sand, and the birthplace of the surf lifesaving movement.

title: Walk the whole Bondi to Coogee coastal path
description: 6km of clifftop path past five beaches and the Waverley Cemetery - do it in October when Sculpture by the Sea takes over.

title: Swim a lap at Bondi Icebergs while waves break over the wall
description: An ocean pool at the south end of Bondi, open since 1929, where the surf washes straight into the lane you are swimming.

title: Ride the ferry and the cable car into Taronga Zoo
description: A zoo on a harbour hillside where the giraffes have a better view of the Opera House than most hotels.

title: Catch the Manly ferry across Sydney Harbour
description: Thirty minutes from Circular Quay for the price of a bus ticket - the best-value harbour cruise in the world.

title: Hike the Manly to Spit Bridge track
description: 10km through harbourside bush, Aboriginal rock engravings and hidden beaches most Sydneysiders have never walked.

title: Watch the Saturday night fireworks over Darling Harbour
description: A reclaimed goods harbour turned promenade of museums, aquarium and restaurants around the water.

title: Explore the Naala Badu building at the Art Gallery of NSW
description: Free entry, and since 2022 a second building including the Tank - a WWII naval oil bunker turned vast underground gallery.

title: Meet the megafauna at the Australian Museum
description: The country's first museum, opened 1827, with dinosaur and First Nations galleries and free general entry.

title: Spend a weekend in the Blue Mountains
description: A World Heritage sandstone plateau split by huge valleys, blue with eucalyptus haze, ninety minutes by train from Sydney.

title: See the Three Sisters lit up after dark at Echo Point
description: Three sandstone pinnacles above the Jamison Valley, central to Gundungurra and Darug stories, floodlit each evening.

title: Ride the steepest passenger railway in the world at Scenic World
description: A 52-degree incline railway built to haul coal, plus a glass-floored cableway over the Jamison Valley.

title: Walk the National Pass at Wentworth Falls
description: A track cut into the cliff face by hand in 1908, running along a ledge halfway down a 187m waterfall.

title: Descend into the Grand Canyon Track at Blackheath
description: A 6km loop into a narrow fern-hung sandstone slot canyon - cool and dripping even in February.

title: Go through the Lucas Cave at Jenolan
description: Among the oldest discovered open cave systems on earth, dated at around 340 million years. Check access - the road has closed for repairs at times.

title: Eat at the art deco Paragon in Katoomba
description: The mountains' main town, full of 1930s guesthouses and cafes, and the base for every walk on the escarpment.

title: Canoe the Kangaroo River through Kangaroo Valley
description: A green valley enclosed by escarpment, with wombats on the flats and a river gentle enough to paddle all day.

title: Watch dolphins from a boat in Jervis Bay
description: A huge sheltered bay with a resident bottlenose dolphin population, and humpbacks passing through in winter and spring.

title: Walk the famously white sand at Hyams Beach
description: Long claimed as the whitest sand in the world - go outside January, when the village is genuinely overwhelmed.

title: Snorkel Green Patch in Booderee National Park
description: A national park owned and jointly managed by the Wreck Bay Aboriginal Community, with the clearest water on the South Coast.

title: Get soaked by the Kiama Blowhole on a big southeast swell
description: A sea cave that fires spray up to 25m into the air - it only really performs when the swell comes from the southeast.

title: Cross the Hampden Bridge at Kangaroo Valley
description: An 1898 sandstone-turreted suspension bridge, the oldest of its kind still standing in Australia.

title: Walk part of the Coast Track in the Royal National Park
description: The world's second-oldest national park, gazetted in 1879 - a 26km coast track of heath, cliffs and empty beaches.

title: Time the tide right for the Figure Eight Pools
description: Rock pools eroded into figure-eights on a wave-swept shelf. People are seriously injured here regularly - only go on a low tide with a small swell, and check the NPWS risk rating first.

title: Jump into the lagoon at Wattamolla
description: A waterfall dropping into a saltwater lagoon behind a beach, in the middle of the Royal National Park.

title: Watch the hang gliders launch at Bald Hill above Wollongong
description: An escarpment city between mountains and sea, with one of Australia's great paragliding launch sites at Stanwell Park.

title: Drive the Sea Cliff Bridge out over the ocean
description: A 665m curved bridge built out over the water after rockfalls closed the cliff road - park and walk the pedestrian lane.

title: Taste aged Semillon in the Hunter Valley
description: Australia's oldest wine region, and the only place making Hunter Semillon - a style that starts thin and becomes extraordinary after a decade.

title: See the Christmas lights at Hunter Valley Gardens
description: Ten themed gardens over 25 hectares, which turn into one of the largest Christmas light displays in the country.

title: Sandboard the Stockton dunes at Port Stephens
description: The largest moving coastal sand dunes in the Southern Hemisphere, 32km long, with camel trains and toboggans on them.

title: Go dolphin watching out of Nelson Bay
description: Around 100 bottlenose dolphins live in Port Stephens year-round, which makes the boat trips unusually reliable.

title: Climb Tomaree Head for the summit view
description: A short steep climb up a 161m volcanic headland with WWII gun emplacements and a view down the whole coastline.

title: Swim at Wategos and watch the sunrise crowd at Byron Bay
description: The most easterly town on the mainland - surf breaks, a hinterland of rainforest, and no longer remotely a secret.

title: Stand on the most easterly point of mainland Australia
description: A 3.7km loop up to the 1901 lighthouse, past the marker for the continent's easternmost point, with whales offshore mid-year.

title: Fish off the breakwater at Brunswick Heads
description: The quieter, cheaper, friendlier town fifteen minutes north of Byron, on a river mouth with a good pub and a good pie.

title: Walk the Wonga Walk through Dorrigo rainforest
description: Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage - a 6.6km loop under strangler figs and past two waterfalls you walk behind.

title: Stand on the Dorrigo Skywalk above the canopy
description: A boardwalk projecting out over the escarpment so you look across the top of the rainforest to the coast 60km away.

title: Climb the Big Banana at Coffs Harbour
description: Built in 1964 and the original Australian Big Thing, now with a waterpark and toboggan run attached.

title: Dive the Solitary Islands Marine Park
description: Where tropical and temperate currents collide - grey nurse sharks, turtles and coral at a latitude that should not have any.

title: Walk the Bathers Way from Nobbys to Merewether
description: A steel city that reinvented itself - 6km of coastal path linking four ocean baths, a fort and a working coal harbour.

title: Swim in the restored Newcastle Ocean Baths
description: A 1922 art deco seawater pool with its famous painted pavilion, reopened after a long restoration.

title: Walk the painted breakwall at Port Macquarie
description: Thousands of individually painted rocks along the breakwall, added by visitors for decades - find a blank one and add yours.

title: Meet the patients at the Port Macquarie Koala Hospital
description: The world's first hospital dedicated to koalas, running since 1973 - free entry, donation-funded, daily feed walks.

title: Climb Mount Gower on Lord Howe Island
description: World Heritage, capped at 400 visitors at a time. The Mount Gower climb is a guided 875m ascent rated among the best day walks on earth.

title: See the summer wildflowers in Kosciuszko National Park
description: Australia's alpine heart - snow gums, glacial lakes and a brief, spectacular wildflower season above the treeline.

title: Stand on the highest point in Australia
description: 2,228m, and unusually approachable - the chairlift from Thredbo puts you within a 13km return walk on a metal mesh path.

title: Ski Thredbo, the longest run in Australia
description: 672m vertical and a 5.9km top-to-bottom run - the most serious ski terrain in the country, and a downhill bike park in summer.

title: Drive the Alpine Way through the Snowy Mountains
description: A mountain road from Jindabyne to Khancoban past the Snowy Hydro scheme, one of the great engineering projects of the 20th century.

title: Stand where the oldest known cremation on earth took place at Mungo
description: A dry lake bed on Barkandji, Mutthi Mutthi and Ngiyampaa country, where Mungo Lady and Mungo Man show 40,000+ years of continuous culture.

title: Walk the Walls of China at sunset
description: A 33km crescent of eroded sand and clay lunettes that glows orange at last light. Access is by guided tour to protect the fossil beds.

title: See the light at Broken Hill, Australia's first heritage-listed city
description: A silver mining town in the far west that became an artists' colony - Pro Hart, the Palace Hotel and a mullock heap over the main street.

title: Watch the sun set through the Living Desert Sculptures
description: Twelve sandstone sculptures carved in situ on a hilltop outside Broken Hill by artists from around the world in 1993.

title: Fossick for black opal at Lightning Ridge
description: The only significant source of black opal on earth, plus free artesian bore baths at 41 degrees and some deeply eccentric buildings.

title: Sleep beside the lions at Dubbo
description: The regional centre of the central west, best known as the base for the open range zoo just outside town.

title: Cycle the 5km circuit at Taronga Western Plains Zoo
description: An open range zoo you tour by bike or cart, with black rhino, giraffe and one of the world's most successful breeding programs.

title: Watch Fitzroy Falls drop off the escarpment
description: An 81m single-drop waterfall over the Illawarra escarpment, in cool-climate country of Bowral, Berrima and Robertson.

title: Get properly remote in Wollemi National Park
description: The largest wilderness in NSW, and where the Wollemi pine - a species thought extinct for two million years - was found in 1994.

title: Switch your torch off in the Glow Worm Tunnel
description: An abandoned 400m railway tunnel near Newnes, now curved, pitch dark and covered in glow worms.

title: Find the ruins of the Newnes shale oil works
description: A ghost industrial site in the Wolgan Valley - brick kilns and retorts from a 1900s shale oil town, slowly going back to bush.

title: Stargaze in Warrumbungle, Australia's only Dark Sky Park
description: Volcanic spires including the Breadknife, and Australia's first International Dark Sky Park, next to Siding Spring Observatory.

title: Swim at Streets Beach, a lagoon in the middle of Brisbane
description: A free man-made sand beach and lagoon on the river opposite the CBD, left over from World Expo 88.

title: Hold a koala at Lone Pine, the world's first koala sanctuary
description: Opened in 1927 and still the largest koala sanctuary anywhere - reachable by river cruise from the city.

title: Watch the city light up from Mount Coot-tha
description: Brisbane's lookout hill, with the botanic gardens, a planetarium and the whole city grid laid out below at dusk.

title: Ride the free CityHopper ferry along the Brisbane River
description: A completely free ferry looping between Sydney Street and North Quay - the cheapest river cruise in Australia.

title: Eat your way through the shipping containers at Eat Street Northshore
description: A riverside night market built from around 180 repurposed shipping containers, open Friday to Sunday evenings.

title: See a contemporary show at GOMA
description: The largest modern art gallery in Australia, free to enter, and home to the Asia Pacific Triennial.

title: Watch the Crocoseum show at Australia Zoo
description: The Irwin family zoo at Beerwah, built around a 5,000-seat stadium for crocodile and free-flight bird demonstrations.

title: Road-trip the Sunshine Coast from Caloundra to Noosa
description: An hour north of Brisbane - surf beaches, a volcanic hinterland and a noticeably slower pace than the Gold Coast.

title: Have breakfast on Hastings Street at Noosa Heads
description: Queensland's most polished beach town, where the main street runs straight onto a north-facing swimming beach.

title: Find the wild koalas on the Noosa National Park coastal track
description: A 5.4km headland walk past Tea Tree Bay and Hells Gates, with koalas in the trees near Tea Tree and dolphins offshore.

title: Learn to surf on the gentle break at Noosa Main Beach
description: One of very few north-facing beaches on the east coast, which makes it unusually calm and ideal for a first lesson.

title: Drive the Glass House Mountains lookout circuit
description: Thirteen volcanic plugs rising abruptly from the plain, named by Cook in 1770 and deeply significant to the Jinibara and Kabi Kabi peoples.

title: Climb Mount Ngungun at sunrise
description: The most achievable of the Glass House peaks - 2.8km return to a ledge looking straight across at Tibrogargan and Beerwah.

title: Walk the Mooloolaba Spit at first light
description: A patrolled beach, an esplanade of cafes and a trawler harbour where you can buy prawns straight off the boat.

title: Swim the calm passage water at Bulcock Beach, Caloundra
description: Sheltered behind Bribie Island, with a tidal current that locals ride like a lazy river on the run-out.

title: See the Gold Coast skyline from the water
description: 57km of surf beach backed by high-rises and canal estates - Australia's most unapologetic holiday city.

title: Look down from the SkyPoint observation deck at Surfers Paradise
description: Level 77 of Q1, and the Climb takes you outside to 270m - the tallest external building climb in the country.

title: Watch the point break from the Burleigh headland at sunset
description: A world-class right-hand point break, a headland national park full of brush turkeys, and the best sunset view back up the coast.

title: Walk the Twin Falls circuit at Springbrook
description: Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage on the rim of an ancient volcano - a 4km track that goes behind two waterfalls.

title: See the glow worms in the cave at Natural Bridge
description: A waterfall pouring through the roof of a basalt cave, whose ceiling fills with glow worms after dark.

title: Walk the treetop canopy bridges at O'Reilly's
description: Ancient Antarctic beech forest on the caldera rim, with 160km of track and a suspended boardwalk 15m up in the canopy.

title: Walk the Tamborine Rainforest Skywalk
description: A plateau of rainforest, wineries and galleries forty minutes from the coast, with a 300m steel walkway through the canopy.

title: Step into the man-made Glow Worm Caves at Tamborine
description: A purpose-built cave housing a glow worm colony, so you can see them in daylight hours and in any weather.

title: Get mobbed by lorikeets at the Currumbin morning feed
description: A not-for-profit sanctuary running a wildlife hospital, famous for the wild rainbow lorikeet feeding twice a day.

title: Ride the DC Rivals HyperCoaster at Movie World
description: Home to the tallest, longest and fastest roller coaster in the Southern Hemisphere, plus a daily parade.

title: Take on the Giant Drop at Dreamworld
description: Australia's largest theme park, with a serious thrill-ride lineup and a genuine tiger conservation program on site.

title: Drop through the Kamikaze at Wet'n'Wild
description: A huge water park on the Pacific Motorway, heated in winter, with a wave pool and a dive-in cinema.

title: Balance under the Pyramid boulders at Girraween
description: Enormous granite domes and precariously balanced boulders in Queensland's cold high country, near the wineries of Stanthorpe.

title: Drive the beach highway on K'gari
description: Formerly Fraser Island - the largest sand island on earth, where the beach is a gazetted road and only 4WDs get on. Butchulla country.

title: Swim in the pure silica sand of Lake McKenzie
description: A perched dune lake sitting on compacted sand and leaves, holding rainwater so pure almost nothing can live in it.

title: Float down Eli Creek on K'gari
description: Four million litres an hour of crystal clear freshwater running to the sea - walk up the boardwalk and float back down.

title: Photograph the rusting Maheno on Seventy-Five Mile Beach
description: A former luxury liner and WWI hospital ship blown ashore by a cyclone in 1935 and slowly disappearing into the sand.

title: Walk the Urangan Pier at Hervey Bay
description: A 868m pier left from an old sugar and timber jetty, on a bay so sheltered it has no surf at all.

title: Have a humpback swim up to the boat in Hervey Bay
description: The world's first Whale Heritage Site - humpbacks stop here to rest with their calves, and often come to inspect the boats.

title: Tour the Bundaberg Rum distillery
description: Distilling since 1888 from the region's sugar cane molasses - the tour ends in the barrel house and the tasting bar.

title: Watch a loggerhead turtle nest at Mon Repos
description: The largest loggerhead nesting concentration in the South Pacific - ranger-guided night visits, November to March. Book ahead.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Lady Elliot Island
description: A coral cay at the southern tip of the Great Barrier Reef, reached by light plane, with resident manta rays year-round.

title: Snorkel the lagoon at Lady Musgrave Island
description: A coral cay ringed by a 3,000-hectare lagoon you can boat right into - camping is allowed, with a permit and all your own water.

title: Surf the northernmost surf beach on the east coast at Agnes Water
description: The Great Barrier Reef blocks swell everywhere north of here, so this is the last real surf beach on the Queensland coast.

title: Watch the sun set over the water at the Town of 1770
description: Named for Cook's second Australian landing, and one of the only spots on the east coast where you watch the sun set into the sea.

title: Straddle the Tropic of Capricorn marker at Rockhampton
description: The beef capital of Australia, sitting exactly on the Tropic of Capricorn, with a spire on the highway marking the line.

title: Hear a choir sing in the Cathedral Cave at Capricorn Caves
description: Privately run limestone caves with famous acoustics, and a chamber where a shaft of sunlight lands only near the summer solstice.

title: Swim the Yeppoon foreshore lagoon
description: The Capricorn Coast's main beach town, with a free stinger-safe lagoon on the foreshore and Keppel Bay islands offshore.

title: Snorkel straight off the sand at Great Keppel Island
description: Seventeen beaches and fringing coral you can swim to from shore, thirty minutes by ferry and far quieter than the Whitsundays.

title: Take the Cape Hillsborough sunrise kangaroo walk near Mackay
description: Wallabies and kangaroos come onto the beach at dawn to feed on mangrove pods - one of the most photographed sunrises in Queensland.

title: Walk the rainforest at Eungella, an island of forest in the dry
description: Rainforest isolated from the coast for thousands of years, with species found nowhere else, an hour inland from Mackay.

title: Wait for a platypus at Broken River, Eungella
description: Purpose-built viewing platforms over a clear river, and the single most reliable place in Australia to see a wild platypus.

title: Base yourself at Airlie Beach for the Whitsundays
description: The mainland gateway to the islands, with a free stinger-safe lagoon and a marina full of sailing boats going out for two nights.

title: Sail the Whitsundays for two nights
description: 74 islands inside the Great Barrier Reef, sheltered enough to sail comfortably and close enough together to anchor somewhere new each night.

title: Walk the length of Whitehaven Beach
description: 7km of 98% pure silica sand that stays cool underfoot in full sun and squeaks as you walk.

title: See the swirling sand from the Hill Inlet lookout
description: The tide pushes white silica and blue water into shifting marbled patterns at the northern end of Whitehaven - go at low tide.

title: Climb Passage Peak on Hamilton Island
description: The most developed Whitsunday island, but a 2.9km climb to 239m gets you above all of it for a view over the whole group.

title: Walk the Living Reef coral lagoon at Daydream Island
description: A small resort island with a free-form outdoor coral lagoon running through the middle of it, holding around 100 species.

title: Swim the Cairns Esplanade Lagoon
description: The launching point for the reef and the Daintree - the town beach is mudflat, so the free saltwater lagoon is where everyone swims.

title: Watch the wading birds on the Cairns Esplanade mudflats
description: An internationally recognised shorebird site - migratory waders arrive from Siberia and Alaska every summer, right beside the boardwalk.

title: Dive the Great Barrier Reef
description: The largest living structure on earth, 2,300km long and visible from space - outer reef sites are far better than the inner ones.

title: Snorkel off the sand at Green Island
description: A true coral cay with rainforest growing on it, 45 minutes from Cairns, where the reef starts a few metres off the beach.

title: Visit the turtle rehabilitation centre on Fitzroy Island
description: A continental island of rainforest and coral beaches, with a volunteer-run turtle hospital and a good climb to the lighthouse.

title: Swim at Four Mile Beach in Port Douglas
description: The comfortable base between the reef and the Daintree. Stinger nets go up from November to May - swim inside them.

title: Stand in the oldest surviving rainforest on earth
description: Around 180 million years old and continuously forested since - Kuku Yalanji country, and the only place the reef meets rainforest.

title: Stand where the rainforest meets the reef at Cape Tribulation
description: Two World Heritage areas touching at one beach. Do not swim - this is estuarine crocodile and stinger country.

title: Take a Dreamtime walk at Mossman Gorge
description: Kuku Yalanji guides lead a smoking ceremony and bush tucker walk through the gorge - the swimming holes are cold and clear.

title: Browse the Kuranda village markets in the rainforest
description: A village on the Atherton escarpment reached by train one way and cable car the other, with markets running since the 1970s.

title: Ride the Kuranda Scenic Railway past Barron Falls
description: An 1891 line hand-cut through 15 tunnels and 37 bridges up the escarpment, stopping at the Barron Falls lookout.

title: Glide over the canopy on the Skyrail Rainforest Cableway
description: 7.5km of gondola metres above World Heritage rainforest, with boardwalk stops on the way - take a glass-floor car.

title: Do the waterfall circuit on the Atherton Tablelands
description: Cool volcanic highlands behind Cairns - crater lakes, dairy country, and a 17km loop linking three swimmable waterfalls.

title: Swim under Millaa Millaa Falls
description: The most photographed waterfall in Australia - an 18m curtain into a round swimming hole, with a shampoo ad filmed here.

title: Explore the ruined Spanish castle at Paronella Park
description: A Catalan immigrant built a mock castle, ballroom and tunnels in the rainforest in the 1930s, powered by his own hydro plant. Now a ruin, lit at night.

title: Look for a cassowary at Mission Beach
description: 14km of palm-backed beach and the best chance in Australia of seeing a wild southern cassowary. Keep your distance - they are dangerous.

title: Stand at the base of Wallaman Falls
description: Australia's highest single-drop waterfall at 268m, with a steep 3.2km track down to the plunge pool and back.

title: Dive the SS Yongala wreck out of Townsville
description: A 1911 shipwreck 90m down the coast, considered one of the best wreck dives in the world - advanced certification required.

title: Walk up Castle Hill in the middle of Townsville
description: A 286m pink granite monolith rising out of the suburbs, walked daily by half the city before the heat comes up.

title: Find wild koalas on the Forts Walk, Magnetic Island
description: WWII gun emplacements at the top of a 4km walk, through one of the densest wild koala populations in northern Australia.

title: Hire a topless Barbie car at Nelly Bay
description: The Magnetic Island ferry terminal, where the local tradition is hiring a brightly coloured open-top Moke to do the island loop.

title: Feed a cassowary at Billabong Sanctuary
description: A small eco-certified wildlife park south of Townsville built around a natural billabong, with hands-on keeper sessions all day.

title: Walk the gold-boom streets of Charters Towers
description: Once so rich it was called The World, with its own stock exchange - the grand arcade and verandahs are still standing.

title: Walk inside the Undara lava tubes
description: Among the longest lava tube systems from a single volcano on earth, formed 190,000 years ago - guided access only.

title: See the Curtain Fig Tree near Atherton
description: A strangler fig that toppled into a neighbouring tree and dropped a 15m curtain of aerial roots - reached by a short boardwalk.

title: Climb Grassy Hill at Cooktown where Cook beached the Endeavour
description: The Endeavour was repaired here for 48 days in 1770 - the town holds both that history and strong Guugu Yimithirr presence.

title: Drive to the Tip of Cape York
description: The northernmost point of mainland Australia - a serious 4WD expedition with river crossings, only passable in the dry season.

title: Watch the sun set into the Indian Ocean from Perth
description: The most isolated major city in the world - closer to Jakarta than to Sydney, and with more sunny days than any other Australian capital.

title: See the wildflowers bloom in Kings Park
description: 400 hectares above the city, larger than Central Park, with a spring wildflower festival showing thousands of WA species.

title: Cross the Elizabeth Quay footbridge at night
description: An inlet cut back into the city to reconnect Perth with the Swan, with a sail-like pedestrian bridge lit after dark.

title: Cruise the Swan River from Perth to Fremantle
description: Derbarl Yerrigan to the Whadjuk Noongar - the river cruise down to Fremantle passes Blackwall Reach and the Swan Valley turnoff.

title: Drink at the Little Creatures brewery in Fremantle
description: A port town of intact 19th-century streetscapes, the Fremantle Markets, and a genuinely distinct identity from Perth.

title: Take the torchlight tour of Fremantle Prison
description: Convict-built in the 1850s and operating as a maximum security prison until 1991 - World Heritage listed, with a tunnels tour by boat underground.

title: See Sculpture by the Sea on Cottesloe Beach
description: Perth's classic beach, with the Indiana teahouse on the sand and a free open-air sculpture exhibition every March.

title: Cycle the whole loop of Rottnest Island
description: Wadjemup - car-free, 22km around, with 63 beaches and 20 bays. Also a place of deep significance as a former Aboriginal prison island.

title: Climb the Wadjemup Lighthouse on Rottnest
description: The first stone lighthouse in WA, at the island's highest point - the climb gets you a view over every bay at once.

title: Take a quokka selfie on Rottnest Island
description: About 10,000 quokkas live here with no natural predators, which is why they are so relaxed. Look, photograph, but never touch or feed them.

title: Wade across to Penguin Island at low tide
description: Home to the largest little penguin colony in WA. The island closes June to September for breeding - take the ferry, the sandbar walk is dangerous.

title: Spot dolphins in the Mandurah canals
description: Bottlenose dolphins live year-round in the Peel-Harvey estuary and routinely swim through the canal housing developments.

title: Meet wild dolphins at the Bunbury Dolphin Discovery Centre
description: Wild dolphins come into the shallows at Koombana Bay of their own accord, with volunteers supervising the interaction zone.

title: Ride the train to the end of the Busselton Jetty
description: 1.8km long - the longest timber-piled jetty in the Southern Hemisphere - with an underwater observatory 8m down at the far end.

title: Taste Cabernet in the Margaret River
description: Under 1% of Australia's wine production but a very large share of its premium bottles - plus world-class surf breaks ten minutes away.

title: Go down into Lake Cave near Margaret River
description: A limestone ridge riddled with caves - Lake Cave has a suspended table formation hanging above a permanent reflecting pool.

title: Surf or watch the break at Yallingup
description: The birthplace of surfing in Western Australia, with a heavy reef break and Ngilgi Cave just up the hill.

title: Walk to the Cape Naturaliste lighthouse and watch for whales
description: The northern end of the Cape to Cape Track, with a whale lookout that catches humpbacks and southern rights on the migration.

title: Stand where the Indian and Southern Oceans meet at Cape Leeuwin
description: The most south-westerly point of the continent, marked by the tallest lighthouse on mainland Australia.

title: Watch whales in Flinders Bay at Augusta
description: Humpbacks and southern rights shelter in this bay in early winter before continuing north - the first stop on the WA whale season.

title: Stand inside a whaling station at Albany's Historic Whaling Station
description: WA's oldest colonial settlement, and the last operating whaling station in Australia until 1978 - now a confronting museum on its own site.

title: Walk out over The Gap on the cantilevered platform
description: A steel walkway projecting 10m out over a 40m granite chasm where the Southern Ocean surges in below your feet.

title: See the Natural Bridge granite arch at Torndirrup
description: A granite span carved out by the Southern Ocean, a short walk from The Gap on the same headland.

title: Walk the Blowholes track at Torndirrup
description: A granite peninsula taking the full force of the Southern Ocean - the blowholes roar through rock fissures on a big swell.

title: Swim in the sheltered water at Greens Pool, Denmark
description: Enormous granite boulders form a natural breakwater, so you get calm, clear turquoise water on an otherwise wild coast.

title: Stand among the tingle trees in the Valley of the Giants
description: Red tingle trees grow nowhere else on earth, reach 75m, and hollow out at the base wide enough to stand a car in.

title: Walk 40m up in the canopy on the Tree Top Walk
description: A 600m steel walkway that sways gently at the height of the tingle canopy - graded for wheelchairs the whole way.

title: Drive the Great Ocean Drive at Esperance
description: A 40km loop past Twilight Beach and Observatory Point, over water so bright it looks colour-corrected.

title: Share the sand with kangaroos at Lucky Bay
description: Repeatedly measured as having the whitest sand in Australia, and the kangaroos genuinely do lie on the beach here.

title: Climb Frenchman Peak in Cape Le Grand
description: A 262m granite peak with a wave-cut cave through its summit, looking down over the whole Recherche Archipelago.

title: See what is left of Esperance's Pink Lake
description: Honest warning: this lake stopped turning pink around 2007 after changes to its salinity. For a reliably pink lake, fly over Lake Hillier or drive to Hutt Lagoon.

title: Stand under the 15m curl of Wave Rock
description: A granite face undercut by 2.7 billion years of weathering into a breaking wave 110m long, streaked by mineral runoff.

title: Find Mulka's Cave rock art near Hyden
description: A granite cave near Wave Rock holding hundreds of hand stencils, and one of the richest rock art sites in the Wheatbelt.

title: Walk among the Pinnacles at dawn
description: Thousands of limestone spires up to 3.5m tall standing in yellow sand - eerie at sunrise, and only two hours from Perth.

title: See the wildflowers around Nambung National Park
description: The park that holds the Pinnacles also carries a spring wildflower display through the heath, plus a good coastal beach at Kangaroo Point.

title: Swim with wild sea lions at Jurien Bay
description: Australian sea lions haul out on the islands offshore, and licensed operators take small groups snorkelling with them.

title: Photograph Nature's Window at Kalbarri
description: A wind-eroded rock arch that frames a bend of the Murchison River gorge perfectly - the most photographed spot on the Coral Coast.

title: Step out onto the Kalbarri Skywalk over the gorge
description: Two platforms cantilevered 25m and 17m out from the cliff edge, 100m above the Murchison River, designed with Nanda Traditional Owners.

title: Walk the Z-Bend River Trail in Kalbarri National Park
description: A ladder-assisted descent 150m down into the gorge to the river - hard, hot, and far better than the lookouts above.

title: See the genuinely pink water of Hutt Lagoon
description: A bubblegum-pink salt lake near Port Gregory, coloured by Dunaliella salina algae - brightest around the middle of the day.

title: See the living stromatolites at Hamelin Pool, Shark Bay
description: World Heritage - stromatolites here are living structures built by cyanobacteria, essentially unchanged for 3.5 billion years.

title: Stand in the shallows for the Monkey Mia dolphin feed
description: Wild bottlenose dolphins have come into this beach every morning for over fifty years, under strict ranger supervision.

title: Snorkel Ningaloo Reef straight off the beach
description: World Heritage fringing reef 260km long, and unlike the Great Barrier Reef you can wade to it from the sand.

title: Base yourself in Exmouth for the Ningaloo season
description: A former US naval communications town at the tip of North West Cape, now the launching point for whale sharks and manta rays.

title: Hike Mandu Mandu Gorge in Cape Range National Park
description: Limestone gorges dropping straight to the reef, with black-footed rock wallabies on the walls in the early morning.

title: Do the drift snorkel at Turquoise Bay
description: Enter at the top and let the current carry you over the coral - get out before the sandbar, the rip past it is genuinely dangerous.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Coral Bay
description: A tiny town on a sheltered bay where the reef starts metres from shore and manta rays are present all year.

title: Swim alongside a whale shark at Ningaloo
description: The most reliable whale shark aggregation on earth, following the March coral spawn - spotter planes find them, you get in with them.

title: Descend into the gorges of Karijini
description: Banded iron gorges cut 100m into 2.5-billion-year-old rock, with class 5 routes that involve swimming and chimneying between walls.

title: Swim at Circular Pool and Fern Pool in Dales Gorge
description: The most accessible Karijini gorge - a rim walk, a steep descent, and a chain of permanent pools along the gorge floor.

title: Swim under Fortescue Falls
description: Karijini's only permanent waterfall, dropping down natural rock terraces into a deep green pool.

title: Find the folded rock wall at Hamersley Gorge
description: On the far side of Karijini, where tectonic pressure buckled the banded iron into visible waves - plus a spa pool above the main one.

title: Watch the iron ore ships load at Port Hedland
description: One of the largest bulk export ports on earth, moving hundreds of millions of tonnes of iron ore a year - the scale is genuinely hard to process.

title: Ride a camel along Cable Beach at sunset in Broome
description: A pearling town with a Japanese cemetery, an outdoor picture garden from 1916, and red pindan cliffs meeting turquoise water.

title: Watch the sun go down over 22km of Cable Beach
description: 22km of sand with no headland to break it, facing due west - the classic Broome sunset, camel trains included.

title: See the Staircase to the Moon at Roebuck Bay
description: A full moon rising over exposed mudflats at extreme low tide creates the illusion of a staircase - only on specific published dates.

title: Find the dinosaur footprints at Gantheaume Point
description: 130-million-year-old sauropod tracks in the reef rock, visible only at a very low tide - check the tide chart before going.

title: See the Horizontal Falls from the air
description: Tides force millions of litres through two narrow cliff gaps, stacking the sea metres higher on one side. Boat transits through the gaps are being phased out - check what operators currently offer.

title: See the Murujuga rock art on the Burrup Peninsula
description: The largest concentration of rock petroglyphs in the world - over a million images, some more than 40,000 years old, on Ngarda-Ngarli country.

title: Walk the Yaburara Heritage Trail at Karratha
description: A 3.5km trail behind town past engravings, grinding stones and shell middens left by the Yaburara people.

title: Swim at Python Pool in Millstream-Chichester
description: Permanent spring-fed pools and palm-lined wetlands in the middle of red Pilbara spinifex country, on Yindjibarndi land.

title: Drive the Gibb River Road across the Kimberley
description: 660km of mostly unsealed former cattle route, with gorges and river crossings the whole way - dry season only, and a real 4WD.

title: Soak in Zebedee Springs at El Questro
description: A million-acre former cattle station on the Gibb, with thermal pools under livistona palms open only in the mornings.

title: Fly over Purnululu National Park
description: World Heritage, and unknown to the wider public until 1983 despite the Kija and Jaru people living alongside it for millennia.

title: Walk into Cathedral Gorge in the Bungle Bungles
description: Orange and grey banded sandstone domes, and a natural amphitheatre with acoustics so good people sing in it.

title: Swim in the infinity pool above Lake Argyle
description: Australia's largest freshwater reservoir by volume, holding around eighteen Sydney Harbours, with 35,000 freshwater crocodiles in it.

title: Watch the sun set over Mirima National Park at Kununurra
description: A town built for the Ord River irrigation scheme, with a miniature version of the Bungle Bungles on its edge.

title: Walk around to Hippo's Yawn near Wave Rock
description: A granite formation shaped like an open hippo mouth, on the same trail network as Wave Rock and far less crowded.

title: Chase the wildflowers through the Perth Hills
description: The Darling Scarp behind the city - jarrah forest, orchards and a spring wildflower season half an hour from the CBD.

title: Walk the old railway tunnel in John Forrest National Park
description: Western Australia's first national park, with a disused railway formation, a tunnel and a waterfall that only runs after winter rain.

title: Spend a weekend in Hobart under the mountain
description: Australia's second-oldest capital, wedged between kunanyi and the Derwent, with more intact Georgian architecture than anywhere else in the country.

title: Do the full lap of Salamanca Market on a Saturday
description: Around 300 stalls along a row of 1830s sandstone warehouses, running every Saturday since 1972 in almost any weather.

title: Take the camo-painted ferry to MONA
description: David Walsh's subterranean museum, cut three storeys into a sandstone cliff and deliberately designed to unsettle you.

title: Stand on the Pinnacle of kunanyi in the wind
description: 1,271m directly above the city, often snow-covered, with a boardwalk over the dolerite boulder field. Take a jacket you think is excessive.

title: Climb Kelly's Steps into Battery Point
description: A hilltop village of mariners' cottages and Arthur Circus, a tiny circular green surrounded by 1840s houses.

title: Eat scallop pie off a punt at Constitution Dock
description: The finish line of the Sydney to Hobart every New Year, with floating fish punts selling straight off the water.

title: Take the ghost tour after dark at Port Arthur
description: A World Heritage convict settlement on a peninsula chosen because it was almost impossible to escape - a heavy, remarkable place.

title: Walk the Three Capes clifftops on the Tasman Peninsula
description: The highest sea cliffs in the Southern Hemisphere, on a dolerite coast of blowholes, arches and the Tessellated Pavement.

title: Take a boat under the cliffs to Tasman Island
description: 300m dolerite columns dropping straight into the sea, with seals, albatross and a lighthouse on top of the island.

title: Explore the pink granite of Freycinet National Park
description: The Hazards - pink granite peaks streaked with orange lichen, between white beaches and dark blue water.

title: Climb to the Wineglass Bay lookout and then walk down to the sand
description: The lookout is a 45-minute climb, but continuing down to the beach itself takes most of the crowd away.

title: Walk the Cape Tourville lighthouse boardwalk
description: A flat 20-minute loop with the best easy view in Freycinet, straight down the coast to the Hazards - and whales in spring.

title: Photograph the orange lichen boulders at the Bay of Fires
description: Named by a navigator who saw Aboriginal fires along the shore - the boulders are covered in a startling orange lichen.

title: Swim at Binalong Bay in the Bay of Fires
description: The southern gateway to the Bay of Fires, and the most swimmable of its beaches - white sand between the orange rocks.

title: Ride the mountain bike trails at St Helens
description: A fishing town turned trail destination, with the Bay of Fires Trail descending 42km from the highlands to the coast.

title: Eat and drink your way around Launceston
description: One of Australia's oldest cities and a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, at the head of the Tamar Valley wine region.

title: Ride the world's longest single-span chairlift over Cataract Gorge
description: A genuine wild gorge fifteen minutes' walk from the city centre, with peacocks, a Victorian garden and a 308m chairlift span.

title: Watch the Japanese macaques in City Park
description: A colony of Japanese macaques, gifted by Launceston's sister city Ikeda in 1980, living in a glasshouse enclosure in the town park.

title: See Cradle Mountain reflected in still water
description: Tasmania's signature peak, in weather that changes hourly - the reflection shot needs a rare windless morning.

title: Walk the Dove Lake circuit under Cradle Mountain
description: A 6km boardwalk loop past the Ballroom Forest and the much-photographed boat shed, with the mountain over your shoulder throughout.

title: Scramble to the Cradle Mountain summit
description: A 13km return climb ending in a genuine boulder scramble at 1,545m - only attempt it in settled weather, which is rare.

title: Walk the six-day Overland Track
description: 65km from Cradle Mountain to Lake St Clair through alpine moorland and rainforest. Booked and fee-paying in the peak season.

title: Take the ferry across Lake St Clair, Australia's deepest lake
description: Glacier-carved and more than 160m deep - the ferry to Narcissus is how Overland walkers finish, and how day walkers skip the flat bit.

title: Watch the sun set over Macquarie Harbour at Strahan
description: A West Coast port on a harbour six times the size of Sydney's, with Hells Gates at its narrow entrance.

title: Cruise the mirror-still Gordon River
description: Tannin-dark water so still it doubles the rainforest perfectly, plus a stop at the Sarah Island convict ruins.

title: Stand on the Franklin River where the blockade happened
description: The 1982-83 campaign to stop this river being dammed changed Australian environmental politics permanently - there is a short riverside walk off the Lyell Highway.

title: Swim in the thermal pool at Hastings Caves
description: Newdegate Cave is the largest dolomite tourist cave in Australia, and there is a 28-degree thermal spring pool at the entrance.

title: Walk the cantilever at the Tahune Airwalk
description: A 597m steel walkway 30m above the Huon River, ending on a cantilevered arm with nothing underneath. Rebuilt after the 2019 fires.

title: Drink cider at the source in the Huon Valley
description: Tasmania's apple country - the Apple Isle name came from here, and the cideries and orchard doors are best at harvest.

title: Eat your way across Bruny Island
description: A short car ferry from Kettering onto an island of cheese, oysters, whisky, fudge and white wallabies.

title: Climb the steps at The Neck for the isthmus view
description: A narrow sand isthmus joining North and South Bruny, with a lookout at the top of the stairs and little penguins coming ashore at dusk.

title: Take the boat under the Bruny Island cliffs from Adventure Bay
description: Three hours in a small boat past the Monument, the Breathing Rock and fur seal colonies - genuinely rough, and genuinely worth it.

title: Visit the Australian Antarctic Division headquarters at Kingston
description: Hobart is a gateway port to Antarctica, and the Division's public display area has expedition equipment and a Hagglunds out front.

title: Wander the Georgian streets of Richmond
description: A whole colonial village preserved - gaol, church, bakery and bridge - twenty-five minutes from Hobart in cool-climate wine country.

title: Stand on Richmond Bridge, the oldest in Australia
description: Built by convict labour in 1823-25 and still carrying traffic - the oldest bridge still in use anywhere in the country.

title: Visit Mount Field, Tasmania's first national park
description: Gazetted in 1916, and unusual in going from tall swamp gum forest to alpine moorland within one short drive.

title: Walk the flat track to Russell Falls
description: A tiered waterfall through tree ferns, reached on a wheelchair-graded path - and a glow worm site after dark.

title: Drive up to Lake Dobson in the snow
description: A glacial lake ringed by pandani, at the top of a rough gravel road - Tasmania's small ski field is just above it.

title: See the fagus turn gold at Mount Field
description: Nothofagus gunnii is Australia's only cold-climate deciduous native, and it turns the alpine slopes rust-gold for about two weeks each autumn.

title: See the hop kilns and poppy fields of the Derwent Valley
description: Oast houses left from the hop industry, and legal medicinal poppy crops that flower across the valley in early summer.

title: See the Yarns silk artwork at Deloraine
description: Four enormous silk panels stitched by 300 people over three years, telling the story of the Meander Valley.

title: Turn the lights off among the glow worms in Marakoopa Cave
description: Mole Creek has the only show caves in Tasmania managed by Parks, and Marakoopa holds the largest glow worm display in any Australian cave.

title: Walk into the takayna / Tarkine rainforest
description: The largest tract of temperate rainforest in Australia, and one of the last strongholds of the healthy Tasmanian devil.

title: Stand at the Edge of the World at Arthur River
description: Looking west from here, the next land is Argentina - the longest uninterrupted stretch of ocean on earth, and the wind proves it.

title: Eat crayfish on the wharf at Stanley
description: A fishing village of colonial cottages tucked in behind a volcanic plug, on the far northwest tip of the state.

title: Ride the chairlift up The Nut at Stanley
description: A 143m volcanic plug rising straight out of the sea, with a 2km loop walk around the flat top and a chairlift if the climb looks too steep.

title: Eat King Island cheese and beef where they are made
description: An island in Bass Strait known for dairy, crayfish, shipwrecks and two of the most highly rated golf courses in the country.

title: Climb Mount Strzelecki on Flinders Island
description: Granite peaks, empty beaches and Killiecrankie diamonds you can fossick yourself, in the Furneaux Group off the northeast.

title: Walk with wombats on Maria Island
description: A car-free island national park, part convict ruin and part wildlife ark - wombats, Cape Barren geese and the Painted Cliffs.

title: Find fossils in the cliff face at Fossil Bluff
description: A sandstone bluff at Wynyard where the oldest marsupial fossil found in Australia was uncovered - shells are still visible in the rock.

title: Meet a Tasmanian devil at Bonorong
description: A rescue and rehabilitation sanctuary north of Hobart that runs the state's wildlife rescue service, with devils, quolls and wombats.

title: Walk the full 10km base loop around Uluru
description: Anangu country. Climbing has been closed since October 2019 at the Traditional Owners' request - the base walk shows you the caves, waterholes and rock art the climb never did.

title: Watch sunrise on Uluru from Talinguru Nyakunytjaku
description: A dune-top viewing area designed with Anangu, where you get Uluru and Kata Tjuta in the same frame as the light arrives.

title: Watch Uluru change colour at sunset
description: The rock runs through ochre, orange and deep red in about twenty minutes as the sun drops - bring something cold and get there early.

title: Walk the Valley of the Winds at Kata Tjuta
description: 36 domes, the tallest 200m higher than Uluru. The 7.4km circuit closes when the forecast passes 36 degrees - start at dawn.

title: Walk into Walpa Gorge between the domes
description: A 2.6km walk up a natural wind tunnel between two of the Kata Tjuta domes, ending at a rare pocket of spearwood and desert bloodwood.

title: Stand at the edge of Kings Canyon
description: 100m sandstone walls in Watarrka National Park, on Luritja land, roughly halfway between Uluru and Alice Springs.

title: Do the Kings Canyon Rim Walk and the Garden of Eden
description: 6km around the canyon rim, starting with 500 steep steps, past beehive domes to a permanent waterhole in a hidden gorge.

title: Spend a few days in Alice Springs
description: Mparntwe to the Arrernte people - a town of 25,000 in the geographic centre of the continent, and the base for everything in the Centre.

title: See a bilby in the nocturnal house at Alice Springs Desert Park
description: Desert habitats recreated against the MacDonnell Ranges, with a nocturnal house holding bilbies, mala and other species you will never see wild.

title: Drive the length of the MacDonnell Ranges
description: A 400km spine of ancient quartzite running east and west of Alice, cut by gorges holding permanent water.

title: Look for black-footed rock wallabies at Simpsons Gap
description: The closest of the western gorges to Alice, with a colony of rock wallabies on the boulders - go at dawn or dusk to see them.

title: Stand in Standley Chasm at midday when the walls glow
description: Angkerle Atwatye - a 9m-wide cleft owned and run by the Western Arrernte, whose walls blaze red for about an hour either side of noon.

title: Do the Ormiston Pound walk and swim at the end
description: A 7.5km loop out through a natural amphitheatre and back down the gorge, finishing at a deep, very cold permanent waterhole.

title: Swim at Ellery Creek Big Hole
description: A permanent waterhole between red cliffs, and the most popular swimming spot in the West MacDonnells. It is genuinely, shockingly cold.

title: Watch the sun set on the cliffs at Glen Helen Gorge
description: Where the Finke River - argued to be the oldest river on earth - cuts through the MacDonnell Ranges.

title: Spend a week in Kakadu National Park
description: Nearly 20,000 square kilometres, World Heritage for both nature and culture, and continuously occupied by Bininj/Mungguy people for 65,000 years.

title: See the rock art and climb to the Nadab lookout at Ubirr
description: Galleries painted and repainted over thousands of years, including a thylacine, above a floodplain that turns gold at sunset.

title: Walk the Burrungkuy (Nourlangie) art site
description: A 1.5km loop past the Anbangbang shelter and the striking Namarrgon, the Lightning Man, repainted in 1964.

title: Take the dawn Yellow Water billabong cruise
description: Saltwater crocodiles, jabiru, sea eagles and enormous numbers of magpie geese - the 6.45am cruise is the one worth getting up for.

title: See the Kakadu wetlands at the end of the wet
description: Bininj people recognise six seasons here. Late in the wet the floodplains are full and green, and the waterfalls are actually running.

title: Do the waterfall circuit in Litchfield National Park
description: Ninety minutes from Darwin and, for swimming, better than Kakadu - four major falls with croc-checked plunge pools.

title: Swim under Wangi Falls
description: Twin falls into a large pool with a sandy edge, the most accessible swim in Litchfield. It closes whenever a saltie is in there - obey the signs.

title: Take the 135 steps down to Florence Falls
